mainTopic: The rule of the מורד and מורדת, and the minimum support a husband gives his wife through a שליש, with the גמרא's calculation of the weekly meals
overview: The amud opens with the last words of a reason from the previous page: the rebellious spouse's payment is set so it does not look like שכר שבת. Then רבי חייא בר יוסף asks שמואל why a מורדת is penalized more than a מורד. שמואל gives two answers: a man suffers more from the lack, and his desire shows outwardly, which adds embarrassment. A new משנה follows. It lists what a husband must give a wife he supports through a שליש: grain, legumes, oil, fruit, a bed, clothing, and a silver מעה. It also sets how much wool she spins for him, eases things for a nursing wife, and says these are minimums for a poor man. The גמרא asks whose measure of a meal fits the two קבין of wheat. Using רב חסדא's rule about the storekeeper's profit, and extra meals for guests and travelers, it shows the amount can fit every opinion. It then explains רבי יוסי's comment on barley as being about the double amount, because the barley of אדום was poor. The amud ends by noting that the משנה leaves out wine, which supports רבי אלעזר. His words come on the next amud.

steps.title: It would look like getting paid for Shabbat
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes an answer from the previous page: the weekly amount is not set to include Shabbat, because that would look like שכר שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: It looks like Shabbat wages.
steps.whatsHappening: These are the closing words of an answer that started on the previous page. The amount for a rebellious spouse is not figured day-by-day including Shabbat, because that would look like being paid for Shabbat.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Being paid for Shabbat is improper. So even a penalty payment is set up so that no part of it looks like money earned for Shabbat.

keyTerms.meaning: It looks like; it appears as
Wages earned for Shabbat, which is forbidden

steps.confusionAlert: This line is not a new topic. It is only the end of a reason that began on the previous page.

phrases.english: It looks like Shabbat wages.
phrases.notes: This finishes a point from the previous page about why the payment isn't counted for Shabbat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends an answer begun on the previous page
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives a reason (avoiding the look of שכר שבת)
steps.terutzMaskana: The amount is set so no money looks like it is paid for Shabbat

steps.title: Why is a rebellious wife penalized more than a rebellious husband?
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא בר יוסף asks שמואל why the law treats a מורד differently from a מורדת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא בר יוסף said to שמואל: What is the difference between a rebellious husband and a rebellious wife?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי חייא בר יוסף asks שמואל a question. Why does a rebellious wife lose more each week than a rebellious husband has to add?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה on the previous page takes seven דינרין a week off a מורדת's כתובה, but adds only three דינרין a week for a מורד. Both refused the same thing, so why is the penalty uneven? This question sets up שמואל's answers.

keyTerms.meaning: A husband who refuses marital relations with his wife
A wife who refuses marital relations with her husband

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר יוֹסֵף לִשְׁמוּאֵל:
phrases.english: Rabbi Chiyya bar Yosef said to Shmuel:
What is the difference between a rebellious husband and a rebellious wife?
phrases.notes: He means: why is the wife's weekly penalty bigger than the husband's?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new question on the same topic of rebellious spouses
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason the מורדת's penalty is larger than the מורד's

steps.title: Look at who pays whom
steps.stepSummary: שמואל answers that in the market of prostitutes, men are the ones who pay. This shows a man suffers more from the lack, so the wife's refusal causes more pain.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Go and learn from the market of prostitutes. Who hires whom?
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל answers with a real-life example. Men pay for relations, not women, which shows a man suffers more when he is refused.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The size of the penalty matches how much pain the refusal causes. A wife's refusal hurts her husband more than a husband's refusal hurts his wife, so her penalty is larger.

keyTerms.meaning: Go out and learn; look at the world and see

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: צֵא וּלְמַד מִשּׁוּק שֶׁל זוֹנוֹת,
phrases.english: He said to him: Go and learn from the market of prostitutes,
who hires whom?
phrases.notes: It is the men who pay, which shows their desire is stronger.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 2
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A man suffers more from lack of relations, so the wife's refusal is penalized more

steps.title: A second answer: his desire shows on the outside
steps.stepSummary: Another answer: a man's desire is visible on the outside, so he also feels embarrassed. A woman's desire is inside and hidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another explanation: his desire is on the outside, and hers is on the inside.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל gives a second, different reason for the same difference. A man's desire can be seen, so he suffers embarrassment too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first answer was about how strong the desire is. This answer is about how visible it is. A refused husband suffers both the lack and the shame, so the wife who refuses pays a bigger penalty.
steps.whatToRemember: A מורדת is penalized more than a מורד for two reasons: a man suffers more from the lack, and his desire is visible, which adds embarrassment.

phrases.english: Another explanation: for this one (the man), his desire is on the outside,
and for this one (the woman), her desire is on the inside.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second answer to the same question
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A man's desire is visible, so refusal causes him embarrassment as well as pain

steps.title: Minimum grain for a wife supported through a third party
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה: a husband who supports his wife through a שליש must give her at least two קבין of wheat or four קבין of barley.
steps.simpleTranslation: One who feeds his wife through a third party may not give her less than two קבין of wheat or four קבין of barley.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It sets the minimum amount of grain a husband must give his wife when someone else hands over her support.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the husband is not living with her, a trusted third party gives her food. The משנה sets a minimum so she is properly fed. Barley is cheaper, so twice as much of it is required.

keyTerms.meaning: A trusted third party who hands over the support

phrases.aramaic: מַתְנִי׳ הַמַּשְׁרֶה אֶת אִשְׁתּוֹ עַל יְדֵי שָׁלִישׁ —
phrases.english: MISHNA: One who feeds his wife through a third party,

phrases.aramaic: לֹא יִפְחוֹת לָהּ מִשְּׁנֵי קַבִּין חִטִּין,
phrases.english: may not give her less than two kav of wheat,
phrases.notes: This is the amount for a week, as the explanation of the משנה makes clear.

phrases.english: or four kav of barley.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ הַמַּשְׁרֶה אֶת אִשְׁתּוֹ עַל יְדֵי שָׁלִישׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a new משנה on a new topic
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Minimum support: two קבין of wheat or four קבין of barley

steps.title: רבי יוסי: barley was only allowed in רבי ישמעאל's area
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי says only רבי ישמעאל allowed barley, because he lived near אדום.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי said: Only רבי ישמעאל, who lived near אדום, allotted her barley.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי adds to the משנה's ruling. He says barley was allowed only because of where רבי ישמעאל lived.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה gives four קבין of barley as an option, double the wheat. רבי יוסי says this ruling came only from רבי ישמעאל, who lived near אדום. The גמרא later explains what he means (steps 33-34).

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי: לֹא פָּסַק לָהּ שְׂעוֹרִין
phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei said: No one allotted her barley

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל, שֶׁהָיָה סָמוּךְ לֶאֱדוֹם.
phrases.english: except Rabbi Yishmael, who was near Edom.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי: לֹא פָּסַק לָהּ שְׂעוֹרִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the barley option from step 5
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only רבי ישמעאל, who lived near אדום, allotted barley (the גמרא explains this as the double amount of barley)

steps.title: Legumes, oil and figs
steps.stepSummary: The husband also gives half a קב of legumes, half a לוג of oil, and a קב of dried figs or a מנה of fig cake. If he does not have these, he gives other produce instead.
steps.simpleTranslation: He gives her half a קב of legumes, half a לוג of oil, and a קב of dried figs or a מנה of fig cake. If he does not have these, he allots equivalent produce from elsewhere.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues listing the foods the wife must receive. If the husband lacks these items, he must provide other produce instead.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Grain alone is not enough. She also needs legumes, oil and fruit. The amounts are set, but the specific foods can be swapped for equal produce.

keyTerms.meaning: Legumes such as beans and lentils
In place of them; an equal amount

phrases.english: And he gives her half a kav of legumes,
and half a log of oil,
and a kav of dried figs or a maneh of fig cake.
phrases.notes: A מנה here is a weight, not a coin.

phrases.english: And if he does not have them, he allots in their place
produce from elsewhere.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the list of required food
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Legumes, oil and figs are also required, or equal produce in their place

steps.title: A bed and mats
steps.stepSummary: The husband must give his wife a bed, a soft mat and a hard mat.
steps.simpleTranslation: And he gives her a bed, a soft mat and a mat.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה moves from food to household needs and lists what she needs for sleeping.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Support covers more than food. It also includes basic furnishings like a bed.

phrases.english: And he gives her a bed, a soft mat, and a hard mat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from food to household items
steps.mimraCoreRuling: He must provide a bed and mats

steps.title: Head covering, belt, shoes and yearly clothing
steps.stepSummary: He gives a cap, a belt, shoes at each festival, and clothing worth fifty זוז each year.
steps.simpleTranslation: He gives her a cap for her head, a belt for her waist, shoes from festival to festival, and clothes worth fifty זוז each year.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה lists the clothing the husband must provide and how often.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each item has its own schedule. Shoes are replaced at every festival, and clothing worth fifty זוז is given once a year.

phrases.english: And he gives her a cap for her head,
and a belt for her waist,
and shoes from festival to festival,

phrases.aramaic: וְכֵלִים שֶׁל חֲמִשִּׁים זוּז מִשָּׁנָה לְשָׁנָה.
phrases.english: and clothes worth fifty zuz from year to year.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues from household items to clothing
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Cap, belt, shoes each festival, and fifty זוז of clothing yearly

steps.title: When to give the clothes, and who keeps the worn ones
steps.stepSummary: New clothes are not given in summer, and worn ones are not given in winter. He gives the fifty זוז of clothing in the rainy season, she wears them into the summer, and the worn clothes stay hers.
steps.simpleTranslation: He does not give her new clothes in summer or worn clothes in the rainy season. Rather, he gives her clothes worth fifty זוז in the rainy season, she covers herself with them when worn in the summer, and the worn clothes are hers.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה explains the timing of the yearly clothing. It ends by saying the old clothes belong to her.
steps.deeperAnalysis: New clothes are warm, so they are needed in winter. Worn clothes are thin, which suits summer. Giving the clothes in the rainy season covers both seasons, and the worn clothes stay with her rather than going back to the husband.
steps.whatToRemember: The husband's support includes set amounts of food, a bed and mats, and clothing. The yearly clothing is given in the rainy season, and the worn clothes belong to the wife.

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵין נוֹתְנִין לָהּ לֹא חֲדָשִׁים בִּימוֹת הַחַמָּה,
phrases.english: And they do not give her new clothes in the summer,
nor worn clothes in the rainy season.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא נוֹתֵן לָהּ כֵּלִים שֶׁל חֲמִשִּׁים זוּז
phrases.english: Rather, he gives her clothes worth fifty zuz
in the rainy season,
and she covers herself with their worn remains in the summer.
phrases.notes: These are the same winter clothes, which are worn thin by summer.

phrases.english: And the worn clothes are hers.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֵין נוֹתְנִין לָהּ לֹא חֲדָשִׁים בִּימוֹת הַחַמָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the timing of the yearly clothing from step 9
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Clothing is given in the rainy season, and the worn clothes belong to the wife

steps.title: Spending money, Friday-night meals, and her earnings
steps.stepSummary: The husband gives his wife a silver מעה for her personal needs, and she eats with him every Friday night. If he does not give the מעה, her earnings belong to her.
steps.simpleTranslation: He gives her a silver מעה for her needs. She eats with him every Friday night. If he does not give her the silver מעה for her needs, the money she earns from her work is hers.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה adds two more things the husband provides: a small coin of spending money, and a seat at his table every Friday night. It also says what happens if he holds back the coin.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now the list covered food and clothing. Now it adds pocket money and eating together on Shabbat. The last line links the coin to her earnings: if he does not give the מעה, he does not get her מעשה ידיה.

keyTerms.meaning: A small silver coin, given as spending money
Her handiwork, meaning the money she earns from her work

phrases.english: He gives her a silver ma'a for her needs.
And she eats with him
from Shabbat night to Shabbat night.

phrases.aramaic: וְאִם אֵין נוֹתֵן לָהּ מָעָה כֶּסֶף לְצוֹרְכָּהּ —
phrases.english: And if he does not give her a silver ma'a for her needs,
her handiwork is hers.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה's list of what the husband provides, after the clothing rules in Step 10.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The husband gives a silver מעה for her needs, and she eats with him every Friday night. If he does not give the מעה, her earnings are hers.

steps.title: How much wool she spins for him
steps.stepSummary: The משנה sets the wife's work amount: five סלעים by weight of warp thread in יהודה (ten in the גליל), or ten סלעים of woof thread in יהודה (twenty in the גליל).
steps.simpleTranslation: What work does she do for him? She spins wool weighing five סלעים of warp thread by the measures of יהודה, which equals ten סלעים by the measures of the גליל. Or she spins wool weighing ten סלעים of woof thread by the measures of יהודה, which equals twenty סלעים by the measures of the גליל.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה now turns to the wife's side: how much work she must produce for her husband. The amount is measured by the weight of wool she spins.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two kinds of thread are listed, and the woof amount is double the warp amount. Each amount is also given in two systems of weights, because a סלע in the גליל counted as half of one in יהודה.

keyTerms.meaning: סלעים, coins used here as units of weight
Warp, the long threads stretched on a loom
Woof, the threads woven across the warp
Two regions of ארץ ישראל that used different weight measures

phrases.english: And what does she make for him?
The weight of five sela of warp in Judea,
phrases.notes: Warp threads are the long ones on the loom. The woof threads in phrase 4 are woven across them.

phrases.english: which are ten sela in the Galilee.

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ מִשְׁקַל עֶשֶׂר סְלָעִים עֵרֶב בִּיהוּדָה,
phrases.english: Or the weight of ten sela of woof in Judea,
which are twenty sela in the Galilee.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Step 11 tied her earnings to the מעה. This step sets how much work she owes him.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: She spins five סלעים of warp in יהודה (ten in the גליל) or ten סלעים of woof in יהודה (twenty in the גליל).

steps.title: A nursing wife works less and eats more
steps.stepSummary: If she is nursing, her required work is lowered and her food is increased.
steps.simpleTranslation: If she is nursing a baby, we lower the amount of work she must do and add to her food.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה makes an adjustment for a wife who is nursing a baby.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both sides of the deal change together. She owes less work, and he gives her more food. The amounts set in Steps 7 and 12 are not fixed for every case.

phrases.english: And if she was nursing,
we reduce for her from her handiwork,
and we add for her to her food.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adjusts the work amount from Step 12 and the food amounts from earlier in the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A nursing wife's work amount is lowered and her food is increased.

steps.title: These are the minimum amounts for a poor man
steps.stepSummary: All the amounts listed are for the poorest husband. A wealthier, respected man gives according to his standing.
steps.simpleTranslation: When were all these amounts said? For the poorest man in ישראל. But for a respected, well-off man, everything goes by his standing.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה closes by explaining that all its numbers are only the minimum.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every amount in the list, from food to clothing to the מעה, is the lowest level, set for an עני. A wealthier husband must give more to match how he lives. This is the last line of the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: In what case were these words said? (a limiting formula)

steps.whatToRemember: The whole משנה gives minimum amounts for a poor man. A richer husband gives more, according to his standing.

phrases.english: In what case are these words said?
With the poorest man in Israel,
but with a respected man, everything is according to his standing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Puts a limit on everything listed so far in the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The amounts are the minimum for a poor man. A respected man gives according to his standing.

steps.title: Whose view does the משנה follow?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whose opinion the משנה follows, and says it is neither רבי יוחנן בן ברוקא nor רבי שמעון.
steps.simpleTranslation: Who is the author of our משנה? It is not רבי יוחנן בן ברוקא, and it is not רבי שמעון.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins by asking which תנא wrote our משנה. It claims the משנה fits neither of two named Sages, and it is setting up a quote that will show why.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is about the food amounts in the משנה. The גמרא says they do not match the measures for a meal given by רבי יוחנן בן ברוקא or by רבי שמעון. The quote in the next steps gives those two measures.
steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not yet giving its answer. It is only claiming that two Sages do not fit. The proof comes in the quote that follows.

phrases.english: GEMARA: Whose is our mishna?
Not Rabbi Yoḥanan ben Beroka,
and not Rabbi Shimon.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַנִּי מַתְנִיתִין, לָא רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן בְּרוֹקָא, וְלָא רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The גמרא opens its discussion of the משנה's food amounts.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא's measure of a meal matches the food amounts in the משנה.

steps.title: The משנה in עירובין: food for two meals
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a משנה in עירובין. An עירוב needs food for two meals for each person. רבי מאיר says weekday meals, and רבי יהודה says Shabbat meals. Both are trying to be lenient.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned: How much is the measure? Food for two meals for each person. His weekday food and not his Shabbat food, according to רבי מאיר. רבי יהודה says: Shabbat food and not weekday food. Both of them mean to be lenient.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts quoting its source, a משנה about how much food is needed for an עירוב. This first part sets up the measures of רבי יוחנן בן ברוקא and רבי שמעון in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An עירוב needs food for two meals for each person. רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה argue about whether a weekday meal or a Shabbat meal is the measure. Each picks whichever he thinks is smaller, so that less food is needed.
steps.confusionAlert: רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה reach opposite answers for the same reason. Each one thinks the meal he picked is the smaller one.

phrases.english: As we learned: And how much is its measure?
phrases.notes: This is a משנה in עירובין about how much food is needed for an עירוב.

phrases.aramaic: מְזוֹן שְׁתֵּי סְעוּדוֹת לְכׇל אֶחָד וְאֶחָד.
phrases.english: Food for two meals for each and every one.
His food for a weekday and not for Shabbat,
the words of Rabbi Meir.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: לַשַּׁבָּת וְלֹא לַחוֹל.
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says: for Shabbat and not for a weekday.
And both this one and that one intend to be lenient.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the quote that backs up the claim in Step 15.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that our משנה follows neither רבי יוחנן בן ברוקא nor רבי שמעון.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה in עירובין about how much food makes two meals for an עירוב.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן בן ברוקא's and רבי שמעון's measures
steps.stepSummary: The quote continues. רבי יוחנן בן ברוקא says two meals are a loaf bought for a פונדיון when wheat sells at four סאין per סלע. רבי שמעון says two meals are two parts of a loaf, when three loaves are made from a קב.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן בן ברוקא says: two meals are a loaf bought for a פונדיון, when wheat sells at four סאין for a סלע. רבי שמעון says: two meals are two parts of a loaf, when three loaves are made from a קב.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting the משנה in עירובין with the two measures it mentioned in Step 15. These are the measures it says our משנה does not match.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each Sage gives a size for two meals. רבי יוחנן בן ברוקא uses a price-based measure, and רבי שמעון uses a measure based on how many loaves come from a קב. Their sizes are different. The גמרא's claim is that the food amounts in our משנה fit neither of them.

keyTerms.meaning: סאין, a unit of volume for grain
A smaller unit of volume for grain

steps.whyThisMatters: These two measures of a meal are the yardsticks the גמרא will use to check the food amounts in our משנה.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan ben Beroka says:
A loaf bought for a pundeyon,
when four se'a sell for a sela.
phrases.notes: He means the price of wheat at that time: four סאין for one סלע.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon says:
Two parts of a loaf,
phrases.notes: "Parts" here means two out of three thirds of the loaf.

phrases.english: when three loaves come from a kav.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן בְּרוֹקָא אוֹמֵר: כִּכָּר הַלָּקוּחַ בְּפוּנְדְּיוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the quote begun in Step 16 and gives the two measures named in Step 15.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that our משנה follows neither רבי יוחנן בן ברוקא nor רבי שמעון.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The measures of a meal given by רבי יוחנן בן ברוקא and רבי שמעון in the משנה in עירובין.

steps.title: The quote ends: smaller amounts for impurity rules
steps.stepSummary: The quoted משנה ends by listing three smaller amounts based on the same loaf: half, a quarter, and an eighth.
steps.simpleTranslation: Half of that loaf is the amount for a house with צרעת. Half of the half (a quarter) is the amount of impure food that makes the body unfit. Half of that (an eighth) is the smallest amount of food that can become impure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting the משנה it started in the last two steps. These lines add three smaller amounts, each a fraction of the same loaf.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These impurity rules are not the point of our סוגיא. They are just the end of the quote. The part the גמרא needs is the size of a meal from the steps before, and it uses that next.

keyTerms.meaning: A house with צרעת (a kind of spiritual leprosy)
To make the body unfit (for eating תרומה)

steps.confusionAlert: Don't get stuck on these impurity amounts. They are only the end of the quoted משנה. The math that matters is the meal size from the previous step.

phrases.english: Half of it — for a house with tzara'at.
And half of its half — to make the body unfit.

phrases.aramaic: וַחֲצִי חֲצִי חֶצְיָהּ — לְקַבֵּל טוּמְאַת אוֹכָלִין.
phrases.english: And half of half of its half — to be able to receive food impurity.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the quote from the עירובין משנה begun in steps 16-17.
steps.raayaObject: The size of a meal according to each תנא
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה in עירובין about the food needed for an עירוב

steps.title: The math fits neither opinion
steps.stepSummary: Two קבין give eight meals by רבי יוחנן בן ברוקא and eighteen by רבי שמעון. Neither equals the fourteen a wife needs.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose opinion is our משנה? If it is רבי יוחנן בן ברוקא, two קבין make only eight meals. If it is רבי שמעון, they make eighteen meals.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to its question from step 15 and now shows the actual numbers. Neither opinion gives the fourteen meals a week that a wife eats.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By רבי יוחנן בן ברוקא, a meal is a quarter of a קב, so two קבין give eight meals, which is too few. By רבי שמעון, a meal is a ninth of a קב, so two קבין give eighteen, which is more than she needs. That is why the משנה seems to follow neither.

keyTerms.meaning: They come out to (this many meals)

phrases.english: Whose opinion is it?
phrases.notes: He means our משנה, which gives a wife two קבין of wheat a week.

phrases.english: If it is Rabbi Yochanan ben Beroka,
they come out to eight!
phrases.notes: At a quarter קב per meal, two קבין are eight meals. She needs fourteen: two a day for seven days.

phrases.english: And if it is Rabbi Shimon,
they come out to eighteen!

steps.triggerLanguage: מַנִּי? אִי רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן בְּרוֹקָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the meal sizes from the quoted משנה to show the math behind step 15's question.
steps.kashyaTarget: The two קבין amount in our משנה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Eight meals is too few and eighteen is too many. Neither matches the fourteen meals she needs.

steps.title: Add a third for the storekeeper's profit
steps.stepSummary: The משנה follows רבי יוחנן בן ברוקא, but part of the loaf's price is the storekeeper's profit, so we add a third.
steps.simpleTranslation: Really the משנה follows רבי יוחנן בן ברוקא. As רב חסדא said, a third of the loaf's price goes to the storekeeper. So here too, add that amount to the meals.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the משנה does follow רבי יוחנן בן ברוקא, once we count the storekeeper's profit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן בן ברוקא measured a meal by a loaf bought in a store. Part of what you pay is the storekeeper's profit, so the loaf holds less wheat than the price suggests. Each meal therefore uses less wheat, and two קבין stretch to more than eight meals.

keyTerms.meaning: Throw it on them, meaning add it to them

phrases.english: Actually, it is Rabbi Yochanan ben Beroka,
and it is as Rav Chisda said:
Take out from them a third for the storekeeper.
Here too:
bring a third and add it onto them.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְעוֹלָם רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן בְּרוֹקָא, וְכִדְאָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 19 by raising רבי יוחנן בן ברוקא's meal count.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Recalculation using an outside idea (the storekeeper's profit)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A store loaf's whole price is wheat, so we get only eight meals.
steps.terutzMaskana: Part of the price is profit, so more meals come out of two קבין.

steps.title: Still only twelve meals
steps.stepSummary: Even after adding the third, there are only twelve meals, not fourteen.
steps.simpleTranslation: But even so, it comes out to only twelve meals!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back: the fix does not go far enough.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Adding the storekeeper's share brings eight meals up to twelve. A wife still needs fourteen meals a week, so two are missing.

phrases.english: Still, they come out to only twelve!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer in step 20.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Twelve meals is still fewer than the fourteen she needs each week.

steps.title: She eats Friday night with her husband
steps.stepSummary: Friday night's meal is eaten with the husband, so it does not come from her weekly portion.
steps.simpleTranslation: She eats with him on Friday nights.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that one of the fourteen meals is not needed from this portion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our משנה is about a husband who supports his wife through someone else. Since she eats Friday night with him, that meal is taken out of the count, so she needs one meal fewer from the portion.

phrases.english: She eats with him on Friday nights.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 21 by lowering the number of meals she needs.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reducing how many meals must be covered
steps.terutzHavaAmina: She needs all fourteen meals from the portion.
steps.terutzMaskana: Friday night's meal comes from her husband, not from the portion.

steps.title: What if 'eating' means marital relations?
steps.stepSummary: The Friday-night answer works only if 'eats with him' is literal. Some explain it as a polite word for marital relations.
steps.simpleTranslation: This works for the one who says it means real eating. But for the one who says 'eating' means marital relations, what can you say?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the Friday-night answer. It does not work for everyone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a view that 'she eats with him on Friday nights' is a polite way of saying marital relations. By that view, she does not actually eat a meal with him, so no meal comes off the count.

phrases.english: This works well for the one who says
it means actual eating.
But for the one who says
'eating' means marital relations,
what can be said?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer in step 22.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If 'eating' means marital relations, there is no meal with him, so the count is not lowered.

steps.title: Even then, thirteen meals are needed
steps.stepSummary: Even if Friday night is removed, she still needs thirteen meals and has only twelve.
steps.simpleTranslation: And besides, she still needs thirteen meals!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a second problem: the Friday-night answer does not close the gap even by its own reasoning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Taking away one meal brings fourteen down to thirteen. The math gave only twelve, so one meal is still missing.

phrases.english: And furthermore, they are thirteen!
phrases.notes: Thirteen meals are needed, and twelve is still one short.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second challenge against step 22.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Fourteen minus one is thirteen, which is still more than twelve.

steps.title: רב חסדא's other version: add a half
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא drops the 'third' version and uses רב חסדא's statement that half the price goes to the storekeeper.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, as רב חסדא said: take out half for the storekeeper. So here too, bring a half and add it on.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a new answer that replaces the 'third' answer. The next step challenges it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If half the loaf's price is the storekeeper's profit, each meal uses much less wheat. Then two קבין come out to sixteen meals, which is enough for fourteen. So the משנה can follow רבי יוחנן בן ברוקא.
steps.whatToRemember: The משנה's two קבין follows רבי יוחנן בן ברוקא, once we count that half of a store loaf's price is the storekeeper's profit. That gives enough meals for the whole week.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows how the גמרא matches a fixed amount in a משנה to a תנא by working out real-life prices, including the seller's profit.

phrases.english: Rather, it is as Rav Chisda said:
Take out from them half for the storekeeper.
So too here,
bring a half and add it onto them.
phrases.notes: This way two קבין come out to sixteen meals, which covers the fourteen she needs.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא כִּדְאָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא, צֵא מֵהֶן מֶחֱצָה לַחֶנְווֹנִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the 'third' answer of step 20 after steps 21-24 showed it falls short.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Replacing the answer with a stronger version of the same idea
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Only a third goes to the storekeeper, which gives twelve meals.
steps.terutzMaskana: Half goes to the storekeeper, which gives sixteen meals. That is enough, so the משנה follows רבי יוחנן בן ברוקא.

steps.title: רב חסדא seems to contradict himself
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא once said the storekeeper adds a third, and now he says the storekeeper takes half. Which is it?
steps.simpleTranslation: This is a difficulty: one statement of רב חסדא contradicts the other statement of רב חסדא!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא just used רב חסדא's rule that half the price goes to the storekeeper. Now it points out that רב חסדא also said the storekeeper only adds a third.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier in the סוגיא, the 'third' version came from רב חסדא. In step 25 the גמרא switched to his 'half' statement. Both cannot be true in the same way, so the גמרא asks how one person can say both.

keyTerms.meaning: One statement of רב חסדא against another of his own statements

phrases.english: There is a difficulty: Rav Chisda against Rav Chisda!
phrases.notes: One statement says the storekeeper adds a third, the other says he takes half.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer just given in step 25 by setting it against רב חסדא's other statement.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב חסדא's statement that half the price goes to the storekeeper.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same אמורא also said the storekeeper adds only a third, so the two statements seem to clash.

steps.title: It depends on whether wood is paid for separately
steps.stepSummary: Where people pay separately for the wood used in baking, the markup is a third. Where they do not, it is half.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not a difficulty. This statement (a third) is in a place where they give money for wood. That statement (half) is in a place where they do not give money for wood.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא settles the contradiction by saying each statement of רב חסדא applies in a different kind of place.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Baking bread needs wood for the oven. If the buyer pays for the wood separately, the storekeeper only needs to add a third. If the wood is not paid for separately, the storekeeper must charge more, so he takes half.

phrases.english: It is not difficult:
this is in a place where they give money for wood,
phrases.notes: This is the 'third' statement. The wood is paid for on the side, so the markup is smaller.

phrases.english: that is in a place where they do not give money for wood.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא קַשְׁיָא: הָא בְּאַתְרָא דְּיָהֲבִי צִיבֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 26.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases (אוקימתא): each statement applies in a different local practice.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב חסדא gave two conflicting figures for the same markup.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both figures are correct. Where wood is paid for separately it is a third, and where it is not it is half.
steps.whatToRemember: The storekeeper's share is a third where wood is paid for separately and half where it is not. This saves the 'half' calculation the גמרא is using.

steps.title: Now there are too many meals: sixteen
steps.stepSummary: Using the 'half' calculation, the amount of food comes to sixteen meals a week. That is more than expected.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, there are sixteen meals.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to counting meals. With the 'half' calculation, it now gets sixteen meals, which seems like too many.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before, the problem was too few meals. Now, with half going to the storekeeper, the count goes up to sixteen. A normal week is six weekdays with two meals each (twelve) plus the שבת meals, so sixteen needs an explanation.

phrases.english: If so, there are sixteen.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Now that the 'half' figure stands, the גמרא checks the resulting meal count and finds it too high.
steps.kashyaTarget: The meal count that comes from using רב חסדא's 'half' figure.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The count comes to sixteen, more than the usual weekly number of meals, so it is unclear whose view the משנה follows.

steps.title: The sixteen fits רבי חידקא's four Shabbat meals
steps.stepSummary: Sixteen meals fits רבי חידקא, who says a person must eat four meals on שבת: twelve weekday meals plus four.
steps.simpleTranslation: Who does this follow? רבי חידקא, who said: a person must eat four meals on שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא suggests that the משנה follows רבי חידקא, and that explains the sixteen meals.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Six weekdays with two meals each make twelve. If שבת has four meals, as רבי חידקא says, the total is exactly sixteen. So the high count is no problem if the משנה follows his view.

keyTerms.meaning: Like whom? Whose view does this follow?

phrases.english: Like whom? Like Rabbi Chidka,
who said: four meals
a person must eat on Shabbat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers an author for the משנה that fits the sixteen-meal count from step 28.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Assigning the משנה to a specific תנא.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Sixteen meals is too many for a normal week.
steps.terutzMaskana: It fits רבי חידקא: twelve weekday meals plus four on שבת.

steps.title: It can also fit the רבנן: one extra meal for guests
steps.stepSummary: Even the רבנן, who say three meals on שבת, can explain sixteen: the extra meal is for guests and travelers.
steps.simpleTranslation: You can even say it follows the רבנן: take away one meal for guests and travelers.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא says we do not have to say the משנה follows only רבי חידקא. It can follow the רבנן too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By the רבנן, the wife needs fifteen meals (twelve plus three on שבת). The sixteenth meal is not for her own eating. It is extra food so she can feed visitors who come by.

keyTerms.meaning: The Sages, the majority view (three meals on שבת)

phrases.english: You can even say the Rabbis,
remove one for guests and travelers.

steps.confusionAlert: The guest meals are not something the wife eats herself. They are extra food the husband must give so the home can feed visitors.
steps.triggerLanguage: אֲפִילּוּ תֵּימָא רַבָּנַן, דַּל חֲדָא לְאָרְחֵי וּפָרְחֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Pushes back on the need to tie the משנה only to רבי חידקא, and gives a way to fit the majority view.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting the count: part of the food is meant for guests.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Only רבי חידקא's four שבת meals can explain sixteen.
steps.terutzMaskana: The רבנן also work: fifteen meals for her and one for guests and travelers.

steps.title: Now even רבי שמעון's eighteen meals fit
steps.stepSummary: Once guest meals are allowed, רבי שמעון's figure of eighteen meals also fits everyone: three guest meals by the רבנן, two by רבי חידקא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now that you have come to this, you can even say it follows רבי שמעון. By the רבנן, take away three meals for guests and travelers. By רבי חידקא, take away two meals for guests and travelers.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא uses the new 'guest meals' idea to also explain רבי שמעון's larger number of meals.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון's amount works out to eighteen meals. By the רבנן the wife needs fifteen, so three are for guests. By רבי חידקא she needs sixteen, so two are for guests. Now the משנה fits every opinion.

keyTerms.meaning: Now that you have come to this (idea)

steps.whatToRemember: The husband's weekly food must include extra for guests and travelers. With that idea, the meal counts of רבי חידקא, the רבנן and רבי שמעון can all be explained.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the wife's food allowance is not just the bare minimum for herself. It also covers normal hospitality.

phrases.english: Now that you have come to this,
phrases.notes: He means the idea from just before: some of the meals are set aside for guests.

phrases.english: you can even say Rabbi Shimon:
according to the Rabbis, remove three for guests and travelers,

phrases.aramaic: לְרַבִּי חִידְקָא — דַּל תַּרְתֵּי לְאָרְחֵי וּפָרְחֵי.
phrases.english: according to Rabbi Chidka, remove two for guests and travelers.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַשְׁתָּא דְּאָתֵית לְהָכִי, אֲפִילּוּ תֵּימָא רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes the 'guests and travelers' idea from step 30 further, to fit רבי שמעון's figure too.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: With extra meals counted for guests and travelers, the משנה's amounts fit רבי שמעון whether he holds like the רבנן (three extra) or like רבי חידקא (two extra).

steps.title: Quoting רבי יוסי on barley
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבי יוסי's line from the משנה: only one sage allotted barley.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי said: Only רבי ישמעאל allotted barley, and so on.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the start of רבי יוסי's statement from the משנה. This sets up the question that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה listed wheat or barley as part of the wife's food. רבי יוסי added that only רבי ישמעאל, who lived near אדום, allotted barley. The גמרא is about to ask what he means by that.

keyTerms.meaning: etc.; the rest of the quote is assumed

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei said:
No one allotted barley, etc.
phrases.notes: The full line in the משנה finishes: except רבי ישמעאל, who lived near אדום.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי: לֹא פָּסַק שְׂעוֹרִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After finishing the calculation of meals, the גמרא moves on to the next line of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only רבי ישמעאל, near אדום, allotted barley for the wife's food.

steps.title: Is barley eaten only in אדום?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי יוסי: does barley get eaten only in אדום and nowhere else?
steps.simpleTranslation: But does that mean people eat barley only in אדום, and in the rest of the world they do not eat it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the plain meaning of רבי יוסי's words. Read simply, he seems to say barley is food only in אדום.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If only the sage near אדום gave barley, it sounds as if barley is not eaten anywhere else. That cannot be right, because people eat barley everywhere.

keyTerms.meaning: אדום, a land near the south of ארץ ישראל

phrases.english: But is it only in Edom that they eat barley,
while everywhere else they do not eat it?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the plain reading of רבי יוסי's statement quoted in step 32.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוסי's claim that only רבי ישמעאל, near אדום, allotted barley
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The plain reading suggests barley is eaten only in אדום, which goes against what we know: barley is eaten everywhere.

steps.title: The point is the double amount of barley
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי means only רבי ישמעאל allotted barley at double the amount of wheat, because the barley of אדום was poor.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what he means: Only רבי ישמעאל, who lived near אדום, allotted barley at double the amount of wheat, because the barley of אדום is poor.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains what רבי יוסי really meant. He was not talking about barley in general, but about giving twice as much barley as wheat.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה gives barley at double the amount of wheat. רבי יוסי says that ratio came from רבי ישמעאל, because the barley near אדום was bad. In other places, where barley is better, she would not need double.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוסי's point is not about whether people eat barley. It is about the double amount, which fits only the poor barley of אדום.

phrases.english: This is what he is saying:
No one allotted barley at double the amount of wheat

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל שֶׁהָיָה סָמוּךְ לֶאֱדוֹם,
phrases.english: except Rabbi Yishmael, who lived near Edom,
because the barley of Edom is poor.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 33 by reinterpreting רבי יוסי's words.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יוסי meant barley was given only in אדום, as if people elsewhere do not eat it.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי יוסי meant only that the double ratio of barley to wheat comes from רבי ישמעאל, because the barley of אדום is poor.

steps.title: Quoting the half קב of legumes
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה: he gives her half a קב of legumes.
steps.simpleTranslation: And he gives her half a קב of legumes.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next item on the משנה's food list. This sets up an observation about what the list does not include.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה continues listing what the husband must give, now legumes. The גמרא quotes this line to point out something missing from the list.

keyTerms.meaning: half a קב, a measure of volume

phrases.english: And he gives her half a kav of legumes.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from רבי יוסי's comment to the next line of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The husband gives his wife half a קב of legumes.

steps.title: No wine on the list supports רבי אלעזר
steps.stepSummary: The משנה does not list wine, and the גמרא says this supports רבי אלעזר, whose statement comes next.
steps.simpleTranslation: Yet wine is not taught. This supports רבי אלעזר, for רבי אלעזר said:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא notices that the משנה's list leaves out wine. It says this supports רבי אלעזר, and begins to quote him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Something left out of a list can teach a lesson. Since the משנה gives legumes, oil and fruit but no wine, the גמרא sees support for a view of רבי אלעזר. His actual words come right after this.

keyTerms.meaning: it is not taught (in the משנה)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not stop here thinking the proof is finished. The גמרא has not yet told us what רבי אלעזר said; it continues right after this.

phrases.english: Yet wine is not taught.
This supports Rabbi Elazar,
for Rabbi Elazar said:

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִילּוּ יַיִן לָא קָתָנֵי. מְסַיַּיע לֵיהּ לְרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a conclusion from the list quoted in step 35, based on what it leaves out.
steps.raayaObject: The view of רבי אלעזר (stated right after this)
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה's food list, which leaves out wine
